inputs.text:
TASK: Produce a source-aligned low-frequency color and tone layer for the first manga page while preserving the supplied line art exactly.

PRIORITY ORDER: 1) immutable source linework, screentones, text, and geometry, 2) no new visual structure, 3) confirmed character palette consistency, 4) complete broad-region colorization. If instructions conflict, follow the higher priority.

SOURCE AUTHORITY: The first input image is the sole authority for canvas, crop, panel layout, whitespace, composition, perspective, anatomy, pose, faces, hairstyle shape, clothing structure, props, architecture, terrain, smoke, effects, every contour, every edge, every screentone dot, hatching pattern, and existing light-and-shadow boundary. Preserve all existing visual boundaries in the same position, size, and shape. Never add, remove, complete, repair, simplify, or redesign content.

LOW-FREQUENCY COLOR ROLE: Fill only regions that already exist in the source. Generate broad, stable color fields and restrained low-frequency tonal separation; do not regenerate high-frequency detail. Treat source grayscale as the authority for structure, texture, and relative luminance, not as a requirement for the final image to remain gray. Preserve dense screentones and distant small characters without reconstructing, enlarging, cleaning, or simplifying them. Keep every color boundary aligned to an existing source boundary.

CHARACTER REFERENCE POLICY: The appended CHARACTER REFERENCE MAP AND PALETTE GUIDE binds each REFERENCE_IMAGE slot to one named character. Apply a named palette only to a confidently matching character already present in the source. Keep stable character colors consistent across panels, and apply outfit colors only when the visible garment structure matches. References may never contribute a pose, face, silhouette, costume shape, prop shape, line, highlight shape, shadow shape, background, or missing body part. If identity is uncertain, do not apply the named palette; color the existing person independently without changing structure.

FULL SCENE COLOR: Fully color every existing non-text region, including characters, props, sky, vegetation, terrain, buildings, interiors, walls, floors, smoke, and effects. Use coherent anime colors, natural skin tones, balanced saturation, clean base colors, readable material separation, and no more than two or three broad tonal levels. Background color must remain independent from character palettes. Do not leave the sky or major background surfaces as a gray wash.

TEXT AND GRAPHICS LOCK: Speech bubbles, caption boxes, narration boxes, signs, labels, logos, and sound-effect regions are immutable source regions. Preserve their exact boundaries and white backgrounds. Copy every glyph, punctuation mark, numeral, letter, stroke, spacing, orientation, and line break exactly from the source. Keep text and black ink neutral black. Do not translate, rewrite, regenerate, move, distort, obscure, or color text.

COLOR APPLICATION: Place color beneath existing ink without shifting edges or tinting black outlines. Follow existing source shading for broad tonal variation. Do not create a new contour, highlight shape, shadow shape, cloud, ridge, mountain, terrain feature, building, object, person, face, limb, clothing detail, or effect line. Avoid painterly rendering, photorealism, glossy effects, dramatic relighting, bloom, rim light, excessive contrast, heavy shadows, and oversaturation.

OUTPUT REQUIREMENT: Return the same manga page with an aligned broad color layer. Source geometry, line art, text, character count, object count, terrain, and scene structure must remain unchanged.
